description: A rehabilitation services manager must decide how to deploy the hospital's only portable powered bariatric lift for the afternoon, with input from a physical therapist and a biomedical equipment coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The hospital has one portable powered bariatric lift available for use today.
shared_context.S2: The medical unit and the surgical recovery unit have both requested the lift for patient transfers.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the final equipment deployment decision and records the related safety and maintenance actions.
shared_context.S4: The hospital's equipment policy requires a safety check and a documented handoff whenever the lift is deployed to a unit.
shared_context.S5: Before the deployment is recorded, Maya holds a routine check-in with physical therapy and biomedical equipment to review the request and any operational details.
shared_context.S6: Once the physical therapy and biomedical equipment representatives have reported during the routine check-in, Maya records the deployment plan without waiting for a representative from either requesting unit.

PF1.text: The medical unit's patient requires the powered bariatric lift for every transfer from 10:00 AM through 6:00 PM today; the standard floor lift cannot safely support the patient's transfer plan, and Dr. Chen completed the assessment this morning before the request was entered.

PF2.text: The surgical recovery unit's currently unavailable lift has a confirmed biomedical repair completion time of 2:00 PM today, after which it can be used for that unit's transfers; Luis verified the time with the repair technician.

acceptance_conditions: The powered lift must be assigned to the medical unit.
The medical-unit deployment must begin at 10:00 AM.
A safety-check commitment for the medical unit must be recorded.
The surgical recovery unit must use its own repaired lift beginning at 2:00 PM.
The surgical recovery unit's repaired-lift plan must be represented in the recorded backup plan.
The medical-unit transfer requirement must be cited as justification for the assignment.

content_checks.C1: decisions['equipment_assigned_to'] in ['Medical Unit', 'medical unit', 'Medical unit', 'medical Unit']
content_checks.C3: any(c['type'] == 'safety_check' and c['target'] in ['Medical Unit', 'medical unit', 'Medical unit', 'medical Unit'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: '2:00 PM' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'] and ('surgical recovery unit' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'] or 'Surgical Recovery Unit' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan']) and ('own lift' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'] or 'repaired lift' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'])
content_checks.C5: '2:00 PM' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'] and ('own lift' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'] or 'repaired lift' in decisions['surgical_unit_backup_plan'])

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The medical-unit assessment changes the assignment to the medical unit, fixes deployment at 10:00 AM, and requires a safety-check commitment because the standard lift is unsafe.
The confirmed repair time changes the surgical recovery plan to use its own repaired lift at 2:00 PM, which must be represented in the recorded backup plan.
